title: Throughput benchmarking harness and methodology (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the current methodology and harness design we use for throughput benchmarking of the serving runtime. It focuses on load generator configurations, repeatability practices, warmup strategies (KV cache & compilation), and the instrumentation/metrics we collect. The goal is to make throughput experiments reproducible and comparable across hardware, model variants, and code changes.

Scope and assumptions:
- Exclusive focus on token generation throughput for autoregressive models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder where applicable).
- We treat latency SLOs and p95/p99 tail behavior separately; this harness prioritizes sustained throughput while recording latency distributions.
- Tests assume a single model shard set unless noted otherwise; multi-model routing/batching is out of scope for this doc.

Definitions:
- Throughput (tokens/s): number of output tokens produced per second aggregated across all workers.
- Effective QPS: number of requests per second taking into account prompt length and sampling settings.
- Sequence length / target tokens: request input length and requested generated tokens per request.
- Warmup: initial traffic phase to stabilize caches, loaded kernels, JIT compilation, and memory allocations.

Harness architecture (high level):
- Controller: orchestrates experiments, config dispatch, experiment metadata, and result aggregation.
- Load generators: stateless processes that send requests to runtime. Support multiple modes: fixed-QPS, fixed-concurrency, closed-loop (send next when previous returns).
- Metrics collector: scrapes Prometheus, GPU metrics (nvidia-smi + DCGM), and system metrics (CPU, mem).
- Profiler hooks: optional sampling profilers (perf, nvprof, Nsight capture) triggered for targeted experiments.
- Artifacts store: S3-compatible bucket for traces, raw logs, and aggregated CSV/json output.

Load generator configuration (recommended fields):
- mode: fixed-qps | fixed-concurrency | closed-loop
- qps: integer (only for fixed-qps)
- concurrency: integer (only for fixed-concurrency)
- payload_catalog: reference to a prompt corpus and distribution file
- sequence_length_distribution: short|medium|long or explicit histogram (e.g., 70% short, 20% med, 10% long)
- sampling: greedy | top_k | top_p | temperature (keep deterministic seeds where applicable)
- tokens_to_generate: integer or distribution
- client_batch_size: number of logical requests batched on client before sending (0 = none)
- arrival_pattern: poisson | constant | bursty (burst size, interval)
- duration: minimum_duration_s and optional max_duration_s
- seed: integer (for deterministic sampling and prompt selection)

Recommended baseline scenarios (to cover common workload shapes):
1) Small requests (short in, small generate): seq_in=32, gen=32, mode=fixed-qps, qps=200
2) Medium requests: seq_in=128, gen=128, mode=fixed-qps, qps=100
3) Long requests: seq_in=512, gen=512, mode=fixed-concurrency, concurrency=8
4) Realistic mix based on production histogram: use payload_catalog and sequence_length_distribution

Warmup strategy (why it matters):
- Warmup stabilizes kernel selection, runtime JIT/compilation, KV cache hot paths, and CUDA context setup. Without warmup, first-minute throughput is artificially low and non-deterministic.
- We recommend a 10-20 minute warmup for heavy models on cold nodes; for microbenchmarks 2-5 minutes may be sufficient.
- Warmup phases:
  - Cold start: bring node up, verify drivers and CUDA/ROCm versions.
  - Model load: load model weights and run a few linear inference passes to force allocation.
  - KV cache priming: for cache-aware serving, send representative prefix requests to populate KV stores (if using prefix caching).
  - Throughput ramp: ramp traffic from 10% -> target over fixed window (recommended 5 minutes).

Repeatability and determinism best practices:
- Fix seeds for any nondeterministic sampling (temperature, top_k/top_p) and note that nondeterministic CUDA kernels or cudnn heuristics can still introduce variance.
- Use the same driver/OS/kernel/CUDA/cuDNN versions across runs (document versions in experiment metadata).
- Pin NUMA/cpu affinity and isolate benchmark host from other noisy processes.
- Ensure identical model artifacts (hashed model tarball) and identical quantization/compilation profiles.
- Repeat each configuration N times (recommended N=5) and report mean+std and median + 95% confidence interval.
- For long-running throughput tests, run multiple independent windows and check for drift.

Instrumentation and metrics to collect (must collect these for every run):
- Request-level: request id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_generated, model_version, route
- Aggregates: tokens/sec global, requests/sec global, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency for request/service time
- Worker-level: GPU utilization %, GPU memory used, power draw, SM utilization, GPU compute/serialize times (if available)
- System-level: CPU utilization, RSS memory, disk IO, network egress/ingress, process-level context switches
- Runtime internals: kernel selection counts, batch sizes accepted by runtime, queue wait times, KV cache hit/miss rates
- Profile samples: periodic nvprof/perf samples and end-of-run flamegraphs (stored in artifacts store)

Analysis and reporting conventions:
- Use tokens/s as primary throughput metric, report also requests/s and average tokens/request so results are comparable.
- Present both aggregated and per-worker breakdowns. For multi-GPU runs show per-GPU tokens/s and balance (max/min).
- Annotate graphs with warmup window, compaction events, OOM or retries.
- For CI regression tests: compare baseline CI-run median tokens/s with new change using relative delta. Flag changes >3% for review and >7% for automatic rollback candidate.

Automation and CI integration:
- Lightweight smoke benchmarks run on every PR: single-node microbench (short seq) timeboxed to 10 minutes.
- Nightly/regression pipeline: full suite across target hardware profiles (e.g., A100-40GB, H100-80GB, T4) with artifact archiving.
- Canary runs: when changing kernels/optimizations, run canary on a small fleet with production-like traffic before rollout.

Known caveats and mitigations:
- Sampling variance: prioritize repeated runs and longer measurement windows for stabilized throughput.
- Driver/cloud instance variability: prefer reserved instances or dedicated nodes for benchmarking.
- Caching effects: explicitly control for cache state (cold vs warm) and document which was used.
- Batch packing interactions: client-side batching and runtime packing can change observed throughput; record client_batch_size and packing thresholds.

Quick example of a canonical experiment manifest (YAML-like, for reproducibility):
- experiment_name: a100-512x512-medium-mix
- hardware_profile: a100-40gb
- model: gptx-13b-8bit
- payload_catalog: corpora/prod-mix-2026-01.json
- sequence_length_distribution: {short: 0.5, med: 0.35, long: 0.15}
- mode: fixed-qps
- qps: 80
- tokens_to_generate: 512
- client_batch_size: 4
- warmup: {duration_min: 15, kv_priming: true}
- repetitions: 5
- metrics_to_record: [tokens_per_sec, p95_latency, gpu_util, kv_hit_rate]

To-dos / open questions:
- Formalize a compact JSON schema for manifests used by the controller (blocked: small schema decisions).
- Add support in loadgen for bursty arrival patterns that mimic production spikes.
- Investigate lightweight kernel-level tracing that can run during CI without heavy overhead.
- Collect more production payload catalogs and ensure anonymization rules.

Appendix: links and references:
- Existing harness code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/main/benchmarks
- Internal PR with recent loadgen improvements: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482
- Prometheus dashboard template: CONFLUENCE-1234

Notes to self / quick scratchpoints:
- When comparing quantized vs fp16 runs, ensure same per-token sampling config; otherwise quality/throughput tradeoffs are incomparable.
- Check poj-42 (JIRA-SERV-289) before final experiments for known memory leak patch.
- Schedule a sync with SRE to reserve nodes for nightly runs.
